record.original_question: Close the gap between the Varshamov-Gilbert existence bound and the linear-programming upper bound for codes.

evidence.quote: The linear programming bound puts restrictions on the maximum dimension of a code given the length and minimum distance using the MacWilliams relations.
Open Question 11.1. Bridge the gap between Varshamov-Gilbert (VG) and Linear Programming (LP) bound.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For positive integers $n$ and $d$ with $1 \le d \le n$, let $A_2(n,d)$ denote the maximum number of codewords in a binary code $C \subseteq \{0,1\}^n$ such that any two distinct codewords differ in at least $d$ coordinates. Define the asymptotic rate function
$$R(\delta) \;=\; \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{\log_2 A_2(n, \lfloor \delta n \rfloor)}{n}, \qquad \delta \in (0, 1/2).$$
Two classical bounds on $R(\delta)$ are:

1. The Gilbert–Varshamov (existence) lower bound:
$$R(\delta) \;\ge\; 1 - H_2(\delta), \qquad H_2(x) = -x \log_2 x - (1-x)\log_2(1-x).$$

2. The linear programming (LP) upper bound: any function $\beta : \{0,1,\dots,n\} \to \mathbb{R}$ that arises as the Hamming-weight enumerator of a code of minimum distance $d$ must satisfy the MacWilliams inequalities, and optimizing over all such functions yields an upper bound $R_{\mathrm{LP}}(\delta)$ on $R(\delta)$. Explicit asymptotic forms (e.g. the McEliece–Rodemich–Rumsey–Welch bound) give
$$R(\delta) \;\le\; H_2\!\left( \tfrac{1}{2} - \sqrt{\delta(1-\delta)} \right).$$

For every $\delta \in (0, 1/2)$, there is a strict gap between the GV lower bound and the LP upper bound. Determine $R(\delta)$ for $\delta \in (0,1/2)$, or more generally close the gap between the Gilbert–Varshamov lower bound and the linear-programming upper bound on $R(\delta)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Determining the true asymptotic rate function $R(\delta)$ for binary codes — equivalently closing the gap between the Gilbert–Varshamov lower bound and the linear-programming (MRRW) upper bound — is widely recognized as a longstanding central open problem in coding theory. Known improvements (e.g. Tsfasman–Vlăduț–Zink for $q \ge 49$ and Jiang–Vardy's asymptotic improvement of GV for linear codes) refine the bounds but do not close the gap, and it remains open whether GV is asymptotically tight in the binary case.

status_evidence.title: Gilbert–Varshamov bound - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Whether the Gilbert–Varshamov bound is tight asymptotically for binary codes remains a major open problem; the best known upper bound is the linear programming (MRRW) bound.
status_evidence.claim: The asymptotic tightness of the GV bound versus the LP upper bound is still open.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic improvement of the Gilbert-Varshamov bound for linear codes
status_evidence.snippet: Jiang and Vardy gave an asymptotic improvement of the GV bound for linear codes, but the result still leaves a gap to the LP upper bound.
status_evidence.claim: Improvements exist but the GV–LP gap is not closed.

status_evidence.title: Problem 7.1: Gilbert-Varshamov Bound (MIT OCW)
status_evidence.snippet: Determining the largest rate possible for binary codes of relative distance δ ∈ (0, 1/2) is a fundamental open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem in research notes.
